tool: NeuroML v2 schema + LEMS language + jLEMS (reference LEMS interpreter) + libNeuroML (Python API)
summary: Retrieved on 2026-09-13 from GitHub REST API, raw repository files (shallow clones in scratch), PyPI JSON, Crossref and docs.neuroml.org. The newest NeuroML v2 schema is NeuroML_v2.3.1.xsd in NeuroML/NeuroML2 Schemas/NeuroML2 (master and development identical; HISTORY.md top entry v2.3.1 dated 2024-08-25; GitHub release NMLv2.3.1 2024-08-20); no v2.4 XSD exists. The LEMS specification is at 0.7.6. Simulation time step is the 'step' Parameter (with 'length', 'target', optional 'seed') of the LEMS Simulation ComponentType; a Meta child can carry 'method' and NEURON cvode tolerances. jLEMS (MIT, release v0.11.1 2024-08-20, commits to 2026-08-31) is documented as the reference LEMS implementation and, per docs, only simulates single-compartment models. jLEMS source contains fixed-step forward Euler and RK4, but RK4 is only applied to state types flattened from Dynamics marked 'simultaneous'; no NeuroML2 core ComponentType sets that flag and LEMS_v0.7.6.xsd does not define it, so standard NeuroML models run through jnml are, by source reading, integrated with fixed-step forward Euler (not yet confirmed by execution). Core current inputs are pulseGenerator, rampGenerator, sineGenerator, compoundInput (sum of children), their dimensionless DL variants, voltageClamp/voltageClampTriple, plus spike-driven inputs (timedSynapticInput, spikeArray, Poisson generators); there is no core chirp, noise-current or arbitrary/time-series waveform input, although users may define new LEMS ComponentTypes. libNeuroML 0.6.7 (PyPI, 2025-06-10) declares no requires_python, targets NeuroML v2.3.1, and has a license metadata discrepancy (package metadata BSD-2-Clause vs three-clause LICENSE text and GitHub detection BSD-3-Clause). Governance: volunteer elected NeuroML Editorial Board (5 editors, staggered 3-year terms) advised by a Scientific Committee; docs licensed CC-BY 4.0.

Multicompartment simulation requires NEURON via jnml/pynml -neuron (separate dependency, not verified here).

reuse_for_neurosem: NeuroML v2.3.1 XSD (bundled in libNeuroML / pyNeuroML) as the structural-validity gate; validate against the bundled XSD, not a file's schemaLocation (official examples still point at beta schemas).

LEMS Simulation files as the protocol execution container: 'step' for numerical refinement (h, h/2, h/4), 'length' for duration, 'seed' for determinism, OutputColumn for recorded voltage, EventOutputFile for spike times.

Core current-clamp inputs: pulseGenerator (baseline with amplitude 0, weak/long/short/hyperpolarizing steps, rebound), rampGenerator (ramp), compoundInput (paired pulses, composites), sineGenerator (fixed-frequency sine); attach with explicitInput or inputList.
libNeuroML read/write/component_factory APIs to implement mutation operators and valid transformations programmatically, and validate_neuroml2 for schema checks.
pyNeuroML LEMSSimulation to generate simulation files and run_lems_with_jneuroml to execute via the bundled jNeuroML 0.14.0 jar (pin the PyPI version and hash the jar).
jLEMS (inside jNeuroML) as the pilot's reference simulator for single-compartment/abstract cell models, as the handoff intends.
NeuroML/LEMS dimensional units system (SI internally) for unit-conversion valid transformations.
docs.neuroml.org schema pages and the verified citations (Sinha et al. eLife 2025; Cannon et al. Front. Neuroinform. 2014; Gleeson et al. PLoS Comput Biol 2010) for background and methods sections.
not_provided_new_for_neurosem: Rheobase search and rheobase-normalised amplitude scaling of protocols (NeuroML/LEMS provide fixed-amplitude inputs only).

Deterministic chirp, frozen pseudo-random current, or arbitrary sampled waveform inputs: no core ComponentType; would need a NeuroSem-defined LEMS ComponentType extending basePointCurrent (with portability checks per simulator) or a piecewise-constant compoundInput approximation.
A protocol-battery abstraction/manifest that instantiates, versions and hashes many protocol variants per model.
Numerical-refinement tolerance calibration, trace alignment to a common time grid, and convergence diagnostics (jLEMS provides only fixed-step output at the chosen dt).

Integration-method control beyond dt for standard NeuroML models in jLEMS (Meta rk4/eulertree does not enable RK4 unless Dynamics are marked simultaneous); any solver-family comparison requires another simulator.
Mutation operators, one-change enforcement, and the mutant classification cascade (invalid, non-executable, unstable, equivalent, non-equivalent, silent).
Behavioural comparison of two NeuroML models (semantic diff / perturbation fingerprint / detection matrix); no model-to-model behavioural equivalence tool was found in the sources examined.
Greedy and random cost-matched protocol selection, split management and held-out leakage barriers.
Run-level provenance records (hashes of model files, jar, environment digest).
handoff_assumption_issues: Numerical mutation family ('solver configuration') under the pilot's 'jNeuroML only' rule: jLEMS is fixed-step, and by source reading standard NeuroML core types never trigger its RK4 path, so a Meta method='rk4' edit is expected to be behaviourally equivalent (no-op). Only the time step (and output sampling) are effective numerical mutations in jLEMS. Confirm empirically in M1.

Forward-Euler integration (inferred) means the h vs h/2 refinement differences for HH-type models may be large; tolerance floors calibrated from |f_h - f_h/2| could be loose, and some models may need very small dt for stable features. Budget runtime accordingly.

'Spatial discretization' mutations, the 'wrong segment group' mutation, and multicompartment models are incompatible with 'jNeuroML only' if that means jLEMS: docs say jLEMS simulates single-compartment models only and multicompartment cells need NEURON (jnml -neuron), a separate dependency.

Protocol 11 (deterministic chirp) and 12 (frozen pseudo-random waveform) have no core NeuroML input type; the handoff's staging is right to defer them, but they are genuinely new NeuroSem code (custom LEMS ComponentType) and their support in exporters such as NEURON is unverified.
Protocol 3 (rheobase search) is not a NeuroML/LEMS feature; it must be an iterative NeuroSem loop over simulations (cost counts toward runtime-matched baselines).

Input timing: pulse/ramp/sine switch via OnCondition tests evaluated during stepping, so onsets and offsets are likely resolved only to the dt grid (inference). Onset/duration mutations and refinement runs should use delays/durations that are exact multiples of every dt level, otherwise refinement itself shifts stimulus timing.

'Current NeuroML validity' should be pinned to NeuroML_v2.3.1.xsd explicitly: docs schema pages are still generated from v2.3 and link NeuroML_v2.3.xsd, and official example files reference beta schemas in schemaLocation.

Version drift in jNeuroML: default (master) branches of jNeuroML and pyNeuroML still reference 0.13.3 while the release/tag pairing is jNeuroML 0.14.0 with pyNeuroML 1.3.22. Freeze via the PyPI release and record the jar hash rather than branch heads.

License audit: libNeuroML metadata (BSD-2-Clause) disagrees with its LICENSE text (three-clause BSD); NeuroML2 core types/schemas are LGPL-3.0 and the LEMS spec repo is GPL-3.0, which matters if NeuroSem redistributes XSDs or core-type files inside its own repository or Docker image.

Valid transformation 'equivalent unit conversion' is constrained by the XSD unit patterns: current quantities accept only A, uA, nA, pA (with optional minus sign), so a conversion to a unit string outside each quantity's pattern would be schema-invalid rather than a valid transformation; enumerate allowed unit strings per dimension from the XSD before generating these transforms.

The handoff lists pyNeuroML/jNeuroML but not libNeuroML or pyLEMS; libNeuroML is the actual Python object model NeuroSem's mutation engine will use, and pyLEMS (explicit Euler) is an alternative Python LEMS interpreter that could serve as a secondary cross-check but not an independent solver family.

The handoff's 'jNeuroML/pyNeuroML: validation' is correct, but schema validity does not cover LEMS-level semantic errors (e.g. wrong compatible component); those surface only at jLEMS build/run time, so the classification cascade needs a separate build-failure category.
uncertainties: The conclusion that jLEMS integrates standard NeuroML models with forward Euler is from reading source at commit 1ae9e8b; no simulation was executed (no Java permitted). Verify in M1, e.g. by comparing an analytically solvable leaky integrator at two dt values.
Whether stimulus onsets are quantised to the dt grid in jLEMS is inferred from OnCondition semantics, not tested.
Whether custom input ComponentTypes (chirp, noise) are supported by the jnml NEURON exporter is unverified.
